page.layout: One printed page (right-hand page of the opening) with a running head at top; one text column of full lines; a woodcut engraving of a spiral shell (umbilicus) inset in the lower part of the column; faint show-through text from the reverse side visible in the middle and right, not transcribed.

main_text.p: ventu. Et post pauca: vidi equidem id ovum mali orbicu-lati modici magnitudine, crusta cartilaginis, velut acetabu-lis brachiorum Polypi crebris insigne. Missis fabulis, de-scriptio cum Icone bellissimè convenit.

Capite 175. tractat Boetius de lapide Carpionum, qui potius officiculum est dicendus, neque in hac historia memorari debebat: sicuti nec oculi Cancrorum, de quibus agit cap. 176. Memini me ab Illustr. Viro Iosepho Scaligero audivisse, singulare esse remedium adversus calculum, si eximantur sole per signum Cancri meante.
main_text.head: CAP. V.

head.i: De Vmbilico marino, lapide Caimanum, & aliis.

main_text.p: DE Umbilico marino agit Boetius cap. 177. qui potius testa est quam lapis & revera operculum testaceorum animantium, & pro diversitate eorum diversæ molis & figuræ. Adiungo Iconem maioris,
plana facie; nam convexa nihil memorabile offendie. De his loquitur Victor de Caligula agens: neque

page.notes: Woodcut of a spiral shell (umbilicus marinus) occupies the lower middle of the column; not transcribed. Show-through from the reverse page is ignored. The faint word at the very bottom left ("prae...") is partly illegible and uncertain. The catchword "que" stands at the right below the last line; the final line "plana facie;nam ... offendie." is printed with a 'D' drop cap at the paragraph start.
